progress_suite.boundary: real local Git; scripted GitHub; no models

verified: Fresh preparation rejects symlinked parent before branch/worktree creation.
Resume preparation rejects symlinked parent before fetch.
Ordinary owner subdirectories cannot inherit parent Git identity and masquerade as candidates.
Recovery requires an exact registered worktree and rejects copied Git pointers and dangling parents.
Dirty candidate contents and index survive resume; owner tracked/untracked bytes, index and HEAD remain unchanged.
limits: Local tests exercise real Git and production controller/recovery functions; a complete deployed dirty-owner issue/PR run remains unverified.
Controllers share Git object/ref storage but have separate working directories and indexes. Owner index, HEAD and file contents are preserved; fetches update remote-tracking refs.
Ownership receipts reject unowned/replaced controllers. A crash before receipt completion leaves a preserved checkout requiring explicit recovery; no automatic deletion.
This does not attest race-proof filesystem isolation against a hostile same-user process.
Targeted CLI execution, Discord initiation/sessions/updates, deployment and live soak remain open.

changes: Production run_once validates deployment at the real deploy checkout, then prepares a receipt-bound controller pinned to fetched origin/main.
Build/resume and sweep use separate lifetime locks. Merge dispatch reconciliation precedes controller preparation so a setup hold cannot hide an uncertain remote mutation.
Candidate and baseline paths resolve through the primary shared Git repository, preserving pre-existing candidate locations.
Cleanup only considers clean registered detached baseline checkouts with HEAD already in origin/main; unknown, ignored, dirty and unmerged work is preserved.
